body:
[aida:product] THE OVERNIGHT AUTONOMY LOOP HAS BEEN DEAD SINCE 02:24 TODAY. I have stopped it and filed BUG-1568. Read this before you count on a drain shipping anything.

WHAT I MEASURED, not what the surfaces said. From .aida/events.jsonl: the last QueueDrained with shipped greater than zero was 2026-09-21T02:24:06Z. Since then, 221 CONSECUTIVE QueueDrained events with shipped=0 and shelved=0, one roughly every four minutes, for about 17.5 hours. Over the same window the launcher log says "launched night-0920 with 24 approved" every single cycle. Both surfaces read healthy. Neither was.

THE ACTUAL ERROR is in the drain logs, not the events:

    error: "a drain is already running (pid 1910690, started 2026-09-21T19:59:15Z, cmd `queue work --auto-complete --batch night-0920`)."

40 of the 40 most recent drain logs died exactly this way, each in about 5-6 seconds with 0 iterations.

IT IS COLLIDING WITH ITSELF. For twelve consecutive cycles I checked, the reported lock holder's start timestamp falls in the SAME MINUTE as that log's own launch, and every one of those holder pids is dead now. There is no squatter and no competing seat - each launch is blocked by something that existed seconds before it and then vanished.

WHY IT SURVIVED A WHOLE DAY, and this is the part worth your attention. The drain does not report the lock refusal as its outcome. It reports:

    x batch `batch:night-0920` drain stopped at BUG-1462 (phase 2 failed)
    -> the rest of the batch is untouched - fix BUG-1462, then re-run

So a lock refusal is attributed to a phase-2 failure of the first pickable batch member. BUG-1462 has nothing wrong with it. Anyone reading the summary - including anyone reading it through aida awaiting or a monitor - is routed to debug an innocent spec. A wrong explanation is worse than none, because none prompts a look.

WHAT I DID: stopped launcher v8 (pid 411600, running 1 day 12:54) after confirming `aida drain status` reported none, so no live work was interrupted. Stopped my own events monitor, which was reporting the same dead loop every four minutes. I did NOT touch the drain CLI - the launcher is behaving correctly given what the tooling tells it.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORKING FROM THIS INVESTIGATION, because both nearly became findings I would have sent you.

1. I first concluded "the queue is empty" and was about to report that as the cause. I had run `aida queue list` as my own shell user while the drain runs `--user role:implementer`. The role queue has 86 entries. That is BUG-89's rule biting me exactly as documented, and I had the memory for it.

2. I also first concluded the batch was exhausted and the launcher was pinned to a stale tag. Wrong - the launcher refreshes the batch every cycle by design, and its own header documents the 2026-09-19 incident that made it do so.

SEPARATELY, AND IT IS YOURS: 28 of the 30 open approved specs have execution_mode UNSET. Only BUG-1481 and BUG-1499 carry drain. `aida why` calls both actionable-ready, and the launcher only selects approved specs whose execution_mode is drain. So even with the lock bug fixed, the drain-eligible pool is two specs deep. Grooming a mode is the advisor write (`aida edit <SPEC> --mode M`) and I have not touched any of them.

CURRENT STATE: 4 open PRs (#2019 mine-pending-your-F3-call, #1999 and #1989 conflicting and fanned, #1978 frozen on Cloudflare Access). All five of the PRs I reworked tonight merged - #2042, #2040, #2035, #2030, #2058.
subject: AUTONOMY IS DOWN and has been since 02:24 — 221 zero-ship drains, drain colliding with its own lock, reported as a phase-2 failure of an innocent spec (BUG-1568); launcher stopped
